# Artifacts register

Tracked, immutable copies of the **measured evidence** that the docs cite as `M` rows live under `testing/artifacts/`; this page is their register.

- One folder per run id (`<experiment>-<UTC timestamp>`), holding the result JSON that
  experiment wrote — and nothing else, unless a doc's `M` claim rests on a file that JSON does
  not contain. Then that file is committed beside it, byte-for-byte, and the Contents row names
  it: `run-20260910-133657/pzt_SandboxVars.lua` is the only one so far.
- Copied into `testing/artifacts/` byte-for-byte at slice close, from the run directory that produced them.
  Verify with `sha256sum`; never hand-edit a file under that directory. The local
  `.gitattributes` sets `* -text` so the committed blob is byte-identical to what the
  experiment wrote — without it `core.autocrlf` would rewrite the CRLF newlines and the
  hashes would not match.
- The **full** run directories — server and client logs, stdout, per-client dumps — stay
  local under `testing/runs/`, which is gitignored (`.gitignore:44`). They are large,
  machine-specific, and regenerated by re-running the experiment.

Why this exists: an `M` grade in `docs/` claims something was measured. That claim has to
be checkable from a fresh clone, so the numbers behind it are committed and the docs cite
these paths rather than a path that only exists on the machine that ran the experiment.

A committed artifact is evidence, not an oracle: a key can be *present and wrong* when the
script that wrote it had a defect. Where that is known, the run's block below lists the key
under **do not cite** and says what to read instead. Nothing here is ever hand-edited to
correct it.

## Script/artifact skew

Standing rule (logged 2026-09-10, program): **when a fix round follows a
slice's last live run, this README notes the skew — the commit that produced the artifact and
what the current script adds — instead of assuming a later run erases it.** Re-running an
experiment for a teardown-only change is poor value; disclosure is what keeps the evidence
honest. Both slice-01 artifacts predate that slice's last fix round, the slice-02 artifact
predates slice 02's, the slice-03 artifact predates slice 03's fix round 1, all three
slice-04 scenario artifacts predate slice 04's, and the slice-05 artifact predates slice 05's
fix round 1 — which added the dataset's `sha256` and dirty flag to `meta`, kept the routed
dataset number as `dataset_routed`, gave the `fluid.script` rows their own transform labels,
narrowed a fluid container's `"n/a"` permission to the six `Food`-only getters and made a
wedged reply a mismatch on every field. The ninth, `exp05b-20260910-093307`, was skew-free
until slice 05's **final fix wave** corrected two of its drift labels and the band they set;
it is listed with the rest, at the end, where it also carries a *do not cite* block of its
own. So all nine are below.

The tenth, **`exp06-20260910-112726`**, and the eleventh, **`exp06b-20260910-120123`**, were
skew-free — each landed in the same commit as the script and the harness command that produced
it — **until slice 06's final fix wave**, which edited both drivers *and* both harness files.
Neither block's measured numbers move, and both blocks now open with a skew note saying exactly
what changed and why (the verdict defect that scored an unmeasured row as a pass, the
`collect()` absent-vs-empty guard, the `item.use` refusal on a depleted item, the tolerance
anchoring, the corrected citations, and a pure move of five helpers into `_common.py`). Both
blocks are also reading guides: `exp06`'s carries three **errata** and two *do not cite* keys —
two of its `summary` keys mislead when quoted alone, one *plan* expectation it was run against
turns out to be wrong, and the scanner has since resolved the two mismatches its `comparison`
block records; `exp06b`'s carries two *do not cite* keys and the reminder that the reduction ran
through the `setCurrentUses` **fallback** rather than through `ItemUser.UseItem`.

The twelfth, thirteenth and fourteenth — **`run-20260910-133657`**, **`run-20260910-133916`** and
**`scenario-20260910-134012`** — were **skew-free** for that same reason (the profiles that produced
them and the artifacts landed in one commit, and the CLI they ran on was already at HEAD) **until
slice 07's final fix wave**, which edited seven modules under `testing/pzt/` — `mods.py`,
`profile.py`, `session.py`, `cli.py`, `scenario.py`, `server.py` and `spikes.py`. `server.py` is the
one that matters here: `merge_sandbox_vars`, the path behind the sandbox `M` of run 1, now keeps a
trailing comment on a rebuilt line and finds the closing `}` at column 0 only; run 1 appended
nothing and its seeded line carries no comment, so nothing it wrote would differ. `spikes.py` only
moved three `took=` sites. **No measured number in any of the three
moves**; every difference is a shape a *future* run would write, and they are listed here rather
than re-run:

- **`took=`.** `server_started` and `client_ready` used to pass the step's own duration as `t=`,
  overwriting the elapsed timestamp every other mark carries. They now pass it as `took=`, beside
  an elapsed `t`. In these three artifacts — and every artifact committed before this wave — `t`
  on exactly those two marks is the STEP's duration, not elapsed time. Read run 1's
  `server_started t=36.6` as "the boot took 36.6 s", never as "36.6 s into the run".
- **`[[verify]]` on the scenario path.** `scenario.run` now runs the profile's probes after
  `client_ready` and records them in `report["verify"]` and the artifact's new `verify` key. The
  scenario artifact below has neither, and its block says so.
- **The artifact's `profile` is the resolved name** (`Profile.name`) rather than the raw
  `--profile` token, so it cannot disagree with `report["profile"]["name"]`. Identical here: the
  run was `--profile mod-under-test` and the name resolves to `mod-under-test`.
- **A RESULT that had no reason of its own now takes the faults.** Run 2's committed
  `result` is the bare `"FAIL"`; the same run today would write
  `"FAIL: mods not found at load: NoSuchModHere"`. The reason is unchanged and is already in
  `faults` in this file — only the RESULT string is shorter here.
- **The `error` mark's `detail` gains its exception type** (`RuntimeError: mods not found at
  load: …`), because `cmd_run`'s `except` widened to `Exception` so that a bus `PermissionError`
  cannot lose `report.json`.
- **A failed probe now skips the hold** on `pzt run` (it used to hold anyway), and `mods.py`
  resolves a mod folder's `mod.info` by parsed version tuple. Neither changes these runs: every
  probe passed, and `KeenPerception` ships one version folder.

The fifteenth and sixteenth — **`run-20260910-151642`** and **`scenario-20260910-151753`** — are
the wave's own acceptance runs, made by the controller on the CLI at `a6b0b54` after the wave
committed and before anything else touched `testing/pzt/`, so they are **skew-free** and are the
first artifacts written in the shapes the list above describes: `client_ready` carries
`took: 37.3` beside an elapsed `t: 54.2`, and the scenario artifact has a `verify` key. Their
blocks are at the end of this file.

The seventeenth, **`exp08-20260910-152944`**, is the first artifact of a different wave: its
driver (`testing/experiments/s08_witness.py`) landed in the same commit as the file (`ba19649`),
and the harness Lua it exercises — the `witness.*` block of `PZTestKit_Core.lua` — was at
`d260671` and clean in the working tree when the run booted, which the artifact records for
itself (`meta.harness_lua_commit`, `meta.harness_lua_dirty`). It writes the `took` shape as well.
It was skew-free until **slice 08's review round 1**, which edited the driver and not the Lua:
`isinstance` guards on four grading blocks, a checked `WITNESS_MAX`, a `getOrCreate` finding
recognised in a string reply as well as a table's `error`, tighter `expected` text on two rows,
and two dead names removed. **Every one of those paths was inert on this run**, so no number in
the file moves and it was not re-run; its block opens with the note. Its block is at the end of
this file.

The eighteenth, **`td1-20260910-192457`**, is slice 09's first teardown session, and it carries
skew of both kinds — a driver fix round and a **harness** one. Its own commit (`e3afaa0`) landed
the driver and the artifact together, on harness Lua at `37e411e` (clean, recorded in the file as
`commit` / `harness_lua_commit` / `harness_lua_dirty`). Then the review round edited the driver
(`4239c5d`, four minors) and the harness (`903ccaa`, two read-backs), with **no re-run**:

- **Driver (`4239c5d`), four edits, none of which changes what a command sent or what a reply
  said** — they change only how the Python side files what came back: a failed re-ask now records
  `reasked` / `first_reply` under `notes` instead of dropping them; the modData exclusion set is
  now per scope (`VANILLA_ITEM_KEYS` for items, `VANILLA_PLAYER_KEYS` for the player — see the
  *do not cite* row below, which is the defect this fixes); `KEYS` is documented as a **display**
  string whose ` | ` is a reader's separator and never a bus token, with a `KEYS_NOTE` in
  `notes`; and the RCON spawn's success is recorded as `rcon_additem_ok` beside the empty
  `rcon_additem` body. **No number in this file moves.**
- **Harness (`903ccaa`), two additions only** — `TK.ITEM_STATE` gained a read-only
  `lastCookMinute` and `item.set`'s ack gained `gameMinute`. The ripple is wider than the three
  server commands: **every `itemState`-bearing reply on both sides gains `lastCookMinute`**,
  because the state table lives in the shared core. This artifact predates both, so every
  `item.get` / `item.set` / `item.update` reply in it simply lacks those keys; `td1b-*` is the
  first artifact that carries either. A diff against a later artifact will show the addition —
  it is an addition, never a changed value.

The nineteenth, **`td1b-20260910-202029`**, is the follow-up micro-session that the same review
round commissioned, and it is **skew-free**: driver and artifact landed in one commit (`38ecf23`)
on harness Lua at `903ccaa`, clean in the working tree, which the file records for itself
(`commit`, `harness_lua_commit`, `harness_lua_dirty false`, `doctor_clean true`). Both blocks are
at the end of this file.

The twentieth, **`td2-20260910-231655`**, is slice 10's teardown session and is **skew-free** the
same way — driver and artifact in one commit (`7453580`) on harness Lua at `291f977`, clean, all
four facts recorded in the file itself. One disclosure that is *not* skew but belongs beside it:
a later residuals commit (`0449fa3`) touched only a **comment block** in `PZTestKit_Core.lua`
(and prose elsewhere) — **no executable path moved**, so the harness this file was measured on
is the harness at `291f977` in every sense that can change a number. It is nevertheless the artifact the next paragraph is
about: it is the first one written on the far side of the rendering change, and no artifact
listed above it can be diffed against it number-for-number.

The twenty-first, **`td3-20260911-001948`**, is slice 11's teardown session and is **skew-free**
in both senses: driver and artifact landed in one commit (`3f4b646`) on harness Lua at `d8cc34e`,
clean in the working tree, with `commit` / `harness_lua_commit` / `harness_lua_dirty false` /
`doctor_clean true` / `acceptance_run` all recorded in the file itself — **and no fix round
followed the run**, so there is nothing to disclose on either side. Its harness addition
(`lua.global`) landed in its own commit **ahead of** the session, as the standing rule requires,
and the acceptance run was its smoke test. Two *driver* notes that are not skew but are worth
knowing before reading the file: `carrier.window_s` records the **requested** 10.0 s while the
probe's own wall stamps give the **measured** 12.54 s, and the `t+3s` tag is a nominal name whose
snapshot actually opened at transmit + 7.58 s. Both are in the block's *do not cite* table.

The twenty-second through twenty-eighth — **`x121-20260911-030023`**, **`x122-20260911-032326`**,
**`x123-20260911-034426`**, **`x124-20260911-035819`**, **`x125-20260911-042055`**,
**`x126-20260911-045205`** and **`x127-20260911-052049`** — are slice 12's seven platform sessions,
and **all seven are skew-free**. Each driver landed in the **same commit** as its artifact
(`6afcb40`, `73e1fd6`, `ef1f678`, `f6c336e`, `6549e4a`, `72b6355`, `5d3f22d`) and **none was edited
afterwards**: `git log -- testing/experiments/x12*.py` shows exactly one commit per driver. All
seven ran on harness Lua at **`5d9633f`**, clean in the working tree, and every file records
`commit` / `harness_lua_commit` / `harness_lua_dirty false` for itself; all but `x123` also record
`doctor_clean true` and their `acceptance_run`. The slice's **only** harness change — the
`text.get` move to `shared/` and its null guard — landed in its own commits **ahead of** the first
session (`ad683fe`, then `5d9633f`), as the standing rule requires, and `x121`'s acceptance run
`run-20260911-024303` was its smoke test.

Three disclosures that are **not** skew but belong beside the list. (i) **`x121`'s first attempt
aborted**, at run id `x121-20260911-025811`: the driver died in M1's grading call
(`TypeError: Timeline.mark() got multiple values for argument 'phase'`) **before any verdict
existed**, no reading of any kind was taken, the run directory was its own copy of the fixture, and
the aborted artifact folder was deleted. The driver was fixed, `doctor` re-run clean and the
session re-run — so the committed driver is the one that produced the committed file, and this is
the opposite of skew. (ii) **`x123` skips `session.verify` by ruling** and says so in its own
`verify_skipped` key: every `[[verify]]` row of profile `x12-loader` is client-side and that
session attaches no client, so each row would have recorded `no client attached` — neither a pass
nor a fail, and not evidence. (iii) a later **comment-only** harness commit (`fefe323`, the
`TK.call` header note that carries x126/x127's correction into the code) moved **no executable
path**, so the harness these seven were measured on is the harness at `5d9633f` in every sense that
can change a number. The slice-12 blocks at the end of this file were written after all seven runs;
they are reading guides, never edits to the files.

One further disclosure, unchanged by the wave and about the harness mod rather than the CLI: a concurrent slice-06 fix round had
`PZTestKit_Server.lua` and `PZTestKit_Server_Recipes.lua` modified in the working tree when these
three ran, so the copies in their run caches are that in-flight text rather than either commit's.
Nothing on the paths these runs exercised is in those two files — `trait.check` is in
`PZTestKit_Core.lua`, `smoke_clock` in `server/scenarios/PZTestKit_Scenario_Smoke.lua`, the bus and
the game-minute scheduler in `PZTestKit_Core.lua` / `PZTestKit_Test.lua`, and all four were at HEAD
— and all three runs recorded `server_errors: 0`. Beside the skew list, these blocks carry the
**provenance a profiled run needs and a plain experiment does not**: the two inputs are the
profile file and the mod folder, so each block records the profile's bytes (they are also in the
artifact's own `profile` block) and which workshop item, `mod.info` id and version folder the mod
was copied from.

A skew entry is about the *script*. Which **dataset** an artifact was measured against is a
separate question, and `exp05-20260910-084109` is the run that shows why: its
`meta.dataset_commit` names a commit the bytes it read were not in. That is a *do not cite*
row in its block, not a skew bullet.

**A skew of a third kind landed in `291f977`, and this is it.** Until that commit
`TK.json` rendered every non-integral number with `string.format("%.6f")`, so **every float on the
bus — in every artifact listed above — is quantised to six decimals**, and none of them supports a
bit-for-bit claim. From `291f977` on, the same branch renders `tostring(v)`, which is
Kahlua's `KahluaUtil.numberToString` → `Double.toString(d)` for a non-integral double and therefore
round-trips exactly; integers are untouched (the `%.0f` branch still takes them first), so no key
changes name or type, and NaN still answers `null` while ±Inf — previously an unparseable ack (C, inferred, not measured) —
answers `null` too. The three candidate formats the deferral named (`%.9g` / `%.10g` / `%.17g`)
were not chosen; the reason is in
[`platform/harness.md#artifacts-discipline`](../platform/harness.md#artifacts-discipline), beside the format
itself. This is a **rendering** change, not a measurement one: it changes the shape of every ack
the harness emits and therefore of every artifact written after it, while everything written
before it — `td1`, `td1b` and all seventeen older runs — stays exactly as recorded and stays
readable at six decimals. **The first artifact written under the new format is `td2-20260910-231655`**
(`teardown-simplestatus.json`, its Contents row below), whose client-side weight readings are
exactly float32-representable while its server-side ones are not — the `d2f`/`f2d` narrowing on
the wire, which six decimals could not have shown; it is also
the first artifact whose `nutrition.get` / `stats.get` replies carry the three
`incWeight` / `incWeightLot` / `decWeight` keys that same commit added.

**`exp03-20260910-045523/body.json`** — produced by `testing/experiments/s03_body.py` at commit
`752d748`. Slice 03's **fix round 1** and its final fix wave changed the script in six ways this
file therefore predates. The rates it carries are unaffected — every fit is `d<value>/d(worldAge)`
and none of the changes touches that — but four keys in it are wrong, and are listed as *do not
cite* below.

- **Row 12 now primes calories per weight** (`CALORIES_FOR_WEIGHT` gained an entry for all
  eleven band weights). This run primed 500 kcal once and swept the weights against it, so
  `updateWeight`'s gain branch — which fires above `1000 + (w−80)·40`, i.e. above −400 at 45 kg
  and above +400 at 65 kg — nudged the low weights off their set points before
  `applyTraitFromWeight` compared them: `rows.r12_weight_bands.bands[].readBack` reads
  **45.0001 / 50.000099 / 55.000099 / 65.000099** against weights 45 / 50 / 55 / 65. **The
  exact-boundary behaviour at 50 kg and at 65 kg is therefore not measured by this file**, and
  the two `match: false` entries are that drift, not a disagreement with the code.
- **`prime()` now writes calories before the weight**, so no window is exposed to the previous
  row's calorie value for the round-trip between the two writes. Visible here as
  `rows.r7_weight_scaling.windows[3]` (the w = 60 window) running at a measured mean weight of
  **60.000757**: its 0.7503 burn ratio is computed against that measured weight, so it stands,
  but the set point did not hold.
- **A failed row now keeps its partial results.** `run_row` used to replace the whole row with
  `{error, traceback}`. That is why `rows.r2_asleep` in this file has exactly three keys: the
  successful `player.sleep true` reply and `heldAtWrite` were discarded by the error handler,
  not missing from the run. (The traceback shows where it really died — `s03_body.py:665` →
  `condition()` → `sample_window()` → `snap()`, i.e. inside the rate window, after the sleep
  write, all eight `prime()` writes and `settimespeed 30` had succeeded.)
- **The movement fit now requires ≥ 4 *consecutive* moving samples**, not 4 anywhere in the
  window. See *do not cite* below.
- **The client mirror is now read at every accelerated window's boundaries.** In this file
  `stats.get` on the client exists only at the session start, around row 1, and in rows 13 and
  14 — there is no client witness for rows 7, 8, 9, 10, 2 or 3–6.
- **The teardown now reads the clock back** (`time_after_restore`, a server-side
  `time.snapshot` after `settimespeed 1`). Absent here, so this run's restoration of the one
  world change it makes rests on the RCON echo in `settimespeed_restored` — which is the admin
  command repeating itself, not the world's state.

  `carbs 180 → 120`, `lipids 84 → 56`, `proteins 26 → 17.333334`, `getCurrentUses() 30 → 20`.
  `Base.MincedMeat` 40/40 and `Base.Cheese` 15/15 both landed on 0 for every macro and for

  alone.** It is the only row whose factor is neither 0 nor 1, and it carries the whole of the
  fractional evidence — seven fields (`hungChange`, four macros, `getCurrentUses()` and
  `getCurrentUsesFloat()`), including the `(int)` truncation that makes `30 → 20` a second,
  integer-valued reading of the same scaling. The other two rows are **boundary rows at factor
  0**: they rule out "one use = one item" and "N is a count of items" — 40 uses of a 40-use tub
  empties it rather than needing 40 tubs — but a model that scaled by *anything* vanishing at
  `used == cur` would satisfy them. Cite all three for the boundary and the Icecream row for
  the fraction.
- **`used/currentUses` is exact only for a whole item.** `getCurrentUses()` is
  `(int)|hungChange × 100|`, so `|hungChange| = cur/100` — and with it
  `1 − used/cur` — holds exactly only while `|hungChange| × 100` is a whole number. On a
  part-spent item the real argument is `1 − ((cur − used)/100)/|hungChange|`, a hair under it.
  Every item here was spawned fresh and `spawn_guard.current_uses_is_whole` checks that per
  row, which is what makes the shorthand legitimate for these three; `factor.float32` (the
  game's own arithmetic, replayed at float32 width) is what the compared expectations use and

  `currentUses` — not `maxUses` — the denominator of any *second* reduction on a part-eaten
  item; the two coincide only while the item is whole, and
  `spawn_guard.current_uses_is_whole` checks that per row rather than assuming it. Do not read

  read 0 before and after, so nothing is hidden by it here.) `hungerChange` moved in lockstep
  with `hungChange` on all three rows only because each item was fresh and uncooked, so the
  read-time ladder is the identity.

**The one finding, and what actually causes it.**
`item_sides_cross_check.getModData.same` is **`false`**: the SERVER's copy of the apple has
`getModData() == {}` and the CLIENT's has `{"customName": "Apple"}` — same instance, same
`#199691187`, six of seven fields identical. The witness read both sides correctly; the
disagreement is in the game.

It is **not** MP item-modData ownership, and `customName` is not client-authored. It is a
**deserialization side effect**, and the jar names it exactly (42.20.4):

- `InventoryItem.setCustomName(Z)V` unconditionally does
  `getModData().rawset("customName", String.valueOf(this.name))` — one `putfield` and then that
  `rawset`, no branch. Writing the *flag* writes the modData key.
- Its call sites are six, and only one is on a path either side took here:
  `InventoryItem.load(ByteBuffer,int)`, `SyncItemFieldsPacket.processClient` /
  `.processServer`, `InventoryItem.createDefaultDeadBody`, `IsoDeadBody.getItem` and
  `CraftRecipeData.createOutputItems`. The last three are corpse and crafting paths; nothing in
  this run is a corpse or a craft.
- The server built the apple **in process** (`additem` → the item factory, never `load`), so its
  table stayed empty. The client received the same item **serialized** and `load()`-ed it, and
  `load` set the flag — which wrote the key.

So the asymmetry is expected for **any freshly `additem`-ed item**, and it is bookkeeping, not
mod data. Three rules follow for slices 09–11:

1. **Say which side you read.** An item's modData is not the same table on the two sides.
2. **Exclude `customName` from any mod-key census.** It is vanilla bookkeeping present on
   every client-side item that came off the wire or off disk, and absent on a server-side item
   that was built in process. It is not evidence of a mod, in either direction.
3. **When item modData does move, it moves wholesale.**
   `SyncItemFieldsPacket.processModData()` calls `getModData().wipe()` on the receiver (when it
   `hasModData`) and then `rawset`s every key of the sender's table into it. A teardown that
   writes item modData on one side loses it to the next field sync from the other that carries
   modData (`setData` sends `moddata` only when the sender item `hasModData()`, and `processModData`
   returns before the wipe when it is null).

How to read it. `trials[0]`–`trials[5]` are the vanilla-trait trials in run order A1, A2, A1, A2, A1, A2:
A1 is `trait.set admin HeartyAppetite add` with no push, A2 is `trait.set admin LightEater add` then
`trait.push admin 2`. Each trial holds `set` (the server step, with `epoch_ms_before` and `epoch_ms_after`,
the python bracket in epoch ms), A2's `push` and `push_wall` (the server's `getTimestampMs` at the push),
`add_poll` and `remove_poll` (the client `stats.get` reads: each row's `snap_wall` is the client's own
`getTimestampMs` at the snapshot and `traitList` its list), and `server_after_add` /
`server_after_remove` (the server's own `stats.get`). Both processes run on one host and share its
clock, so a client `snap_wall` minus a server-side stamp is a latency. The server executes a command and
writes its acknowledgement in the same call, and the driver sees the acknowledgement at most about
0.25 s later, so a write lies in the last 0.25 s of its `set` bracket; the server picked commands up
0.26–2.02 s after they were sent (it polls its command file every 20 ticks). `phases.A3` is the
registered trait: `route_probe` (the server's `ResourceLocation.of` global and the client's registry
object), the grant (`moddata.set admin TKX_grant TKX:Probe`), `grants_polls`, the push key, `add_poll`,
`server_after_add`, `lastId`, then the removal. An empty Lua list serialises as `{}`, not `[]`.

- **A1, no push** (`trials[0]`, `[2]`, `[4]`): the server's list held `heartyappetite` after each add
  (the first non-empty trait list any run has read), and the client's first read holding it came 0.511,
  0.562 and 0.417 s after the add's acknowledgement was seen; the read before it, where there was one,
  came 0.010 and 0.062 s after. Removal, no push: the first client read without it came 0.469, 0.527 and
  1.141 s after the removal's acknowledgement, and in `trials[4]` the client still held it at 0.639 s.
- **A2, push** (`trials[1]`, `[3]`, `[5]`): the server ran the push 1.21, 1.36 and 1.56 s after the
  add's acknowledgement, and the client's first read after the push, 0.18–0.37 s after its stamp,
  already held `lighteater` each time. The push and the experience packet are not separated.
- **A3, registered trait**: `ResourceLocation.of` is a function on the server, so the probe's resolver
  took the `ResourceLocation` branch; `grants` read 1 at the first poll, 1.26 s after the grant's
  acknowledgement, and `lastId` `TKX:Probe`. Server and client lists both read `probe` (the id's path,
  without `tkx:`), the client's first read holding it 3.72 s after the grant's acknowledgement (the
  server's 2 s pickup of the push key sat between). The removal (`lastId` `-TKX:Probe`, `removes` 1)
  left both lists empty.

`TKX_TraitProbe`; the fixture's own sandbox, `DayLength` 4, a 90-minute day). Both `[[verify]]` rows
passed (`SWTraits.traits` resolved with 32 keys; the probe's `version` 1), no mod was missing,

How to read it. `arms.a`–`arms.f` are six 60 s idle arms in run order: `a` weight 75 trait absent, `b`
weight 75 trait held, `c`/`d` the same at 85, `e`/`f` at 80. Each row is one server `stats.get admin`:
`wall` is the server's own `getTimestampMs` at the snapshot (the series' clock), `calories`, `weight`,
`running`, `sprinting` and `traitList` (`held` is the driver's test for `adaptivemetabolism` in it).
`phases.W75`/`W85`/`W80` hold each pair's writes: `weight_set` and `cal_set_absent`/`cal_set_held`
(server `nutrition.set`, each with its `nutrition.get` read back), the grant
(`moddata.set admin TKX_grant SWTraits:SWAdaptiveMetabolism`) and `grant_wait` (server reads until the
list held it), the removal and `remove_wait`. `phases.summary.<pair>` is the grading: `slope_absent` and
`slope_held` (least squares, kcal per second on the server's clock), `slope_diff`, `absent_residuals`
and `held_residuals` (each poll interval's calorie change less the control's slope times its length),
`held_steps` (the intervals whose residual exceeds `step_floor_used`), `step_spacing_s` (for each pair
of consecutive steps, `lo` and `hi` bound the true spacing, since a step lies anywhere inside its
interval) and `cadence_mean_s`. The server polls were about 1.3 s apart.

- **The write reaches the store.** Weight 75: twelve steps of 0.3319–0.3339 kcal (median 0.3332), mean
  cadence 5.01 s; the held slope -0.1749 against -0.2404 absent (+0.0655 kcal/s). Weight 85: twelve
  steps of -0.3313 to -0.3355 (median -0.3347), mean cadence 5.09 s; -0.3388 against -0.2724
  (-0.0665). Every `step_spacing_s` bracket holds 5 s. Predicted: 60 / 90 × 0.5 = 0.3333 kcal per 5 s.
- **The dead band.** Weight 80: held -0.25664 against absent -0.25673, no step.
- **The controls.** No trait-absent arm showed a step (`control_steps` 0, residual spread 0.001–0.002
  kcal); the three absent slopes stand as the weights over 80 (0.937 and 1.061 against 0.9375 and
  1.0625). The grant held at the first read after it each time, and every removal left the list empty
  (`TKX_TraitProbe.grants` 3, `removes` 3).

serial boots** of the golden fixture: `boots.takeover` (`nr-takeover`, Mode 1) runs the mod's
`CalculateStats` handler instead of vanilla's seven stat updaters; `boots.overlay` (`nr-overlay`,
Mode 2) runs the seven updaters as the control. `doctor_clean true`, harness Lua `42425e9` clean,
build 42.20.4; `summary.verify_ok` `[true, true, true, true]` on both boots, `mods_not_found` empty on

How to read it. Three phases, their verdicts in `verdicts`. **P1** (`phases.P1`) is the headline:
`bench.global NutritionRevamp.bench_fast 100000` on the takeover server returned `usPerCall 3.06`
(`ms 306` / `n 100000`) — the per-call wall cost of one whole fast-kernel step through the mod's entry
point. `bench_fast` fills one representative **steady-state awake** tick with every trait and flag
false, so the step takes its cheapest awake branch (the asleep, the stress-from-wounds/infection/
hemophobia and the idle-increment arms are not exercised; the not-deaf sound-stress arm and all seven
stat writes do run): the reading is a representative **floor** of the typical per-tick handler cost,
not a worst case. **P2** (`phases.P2`) is a **method note, not a measurement**: `bench.global
NutritionRevamp.kernel.fast.step 100000` calls the step with no arguments, so it raises on `inp.M` at
`NR_Kernel_Fast.lua:69` and `bench.global`'s own `pcall` catches it (`ack.calls 0`, `ack.error` set,
`ack.usPerCall 0.02` the cost of entering and catching the raise) — which is exactly why Task 2
exposed `bench_fast` as the step's benchable proxy. **P3** (`phases.P3`) reads `tick.rate 10` on each
boot server-side: takeover `10.01` ticks/s, overlay `10.10` ticks/s, `takeover_over_overlay 0.990` —
the handler holds the server tick rate within about 1 % of the seven updaters it replaces. The
absolute ~10 ticks/s is this host's own server OnTick cadence; the comparison is the ratio.

- **The entry-gate verdict** (`verdicts.ENTRY_GATE`, `summary.entry_gate`) is **`proceed`**: the
  per-call cost (3.06 µs) is within the ≤ 50 µs budget and takeover's tick rate tracks overlay's
  (≥ 90 %), so takeover stays the shipped default and Plan 2 runs as written. Had either failed, the
  overlay-default finding would have changed only the shipped mode and the § 6 claim (read by Task 11
  and Task 17), never the plan's other tasks — the engine is built either way.
- **The takeover boot's `server_error_count 7` is the P2 probe, not a fault.** The seven are the
  deliberate no-argument `kernel.fast.step` bench raising at `NR_Kernel_Fast.lua:69`, caught by
  `bench.global`'s `pcall`, plus the Kahlua `flushErrorMessage` / `STACK TRACE` lines the server error
  collector counts; the overlay boot, which runs no P2 probe, has `server_error_count 0`, and P1 and
  P3 on the takeover boot are clean.

How to read it. The probe zeroes `ThirstIncrease` and `ThirstSleepingIncrease` at file scope and `HungerIncrease`, `HungerIncreaseWhileAsleep`, `HungerIncreaseWhenExercise` and `FatigueIncrease` in an `OnGameBoot` handler, and keeps string fields in the global `TKX_G` (`phases.A`). The Lua table is a mirror once `ZomboidGlobals.Load` has run, so `phases.A`'s table reads say what Lua held, and the drift in B, B2, D and E says what the Java statics held. Each game minute, on the server, the probe reads each online player's three stats (pre), writes 0.3, 0.2 and 0.1 through `stats:set(CharacterStat.X, v)` and reads them back (post); a ring row per player per minute carries `d = pre − that player's previous post` (`phases.<P>.ring.rows`; `verdicts.<P>.observed.ring` summarises them per user, split by the server's `isAsleep` at the minute; `agg` is the probe's own per-user maximum |d| over the phase).

The day-boundary arms fast-forward with `settimespeed 30` to 05:30–06:25 (`phases.db_*.ff_polls`), go back to `settimespeed 1`, load 58 fed ghosts and read the ring from about 05:52 to past 07:08; `summaries.db_*.close` interpolates the 07:00 epoch from two time snapshots (`phases.db_*.snap0`, `snap1`) and reads the frames that start within two game minutes of it. Deviation: each day-boundary arm holds 515 kept frames (`summaries.db_budget10.frames`, `summaries.db_burst.frames`), under H3's sizing rule of at least 1000 frames an arm.

- **A/B** (3034 frames a side): empty 4972 ms busy less 384 ghost ms, 1.512 ms a frame; none 4747 ms, 1.565 ms a frame; −0.052 ms a frame by the totals, −0.077 by the quiet frames (2550 and 2549 frames). The pairs read −0.238 (`empty1`−`none1`) and +0.133 (`empty2`−`none2`) by the totals; the four arms read 1.873, 1.635, 1.389 and 1.256 ms a frame in order, the empty arms net of their ghost ms (`summaries.<arm>.busy_sum` less `ghostMs_sum`, over `frames`; 1.753 and 1.525 with them), a drift of about 0.6 ms a frame over the 10 minutes; a fit of a linear drift plus the empty offset to the four reads −0.053 ms a frame with residuals of at most 0.018 (inference); the fit has one degree of freedom, so the 0.018 is the curvature a linear drift cannot absorb, not an error bar, and the offset's standard error is about 0.03 ms. The bound (0.1 ms a frame) is weakly supported, not contradicted and not resolved.

The client side: before each arm both clients armed `world.posring 20000 pace ±6` (the sign alternating arm by arm, `phases.<arm>.pace_dx`) and after the server's reads wrote their rings to `posring/`; `summaries.clients.<arm>.<user>` reads the client frames inside the server ring's kept span: `stamp` (gaps between successive distinct `getLastRemoteUpdate()` stamps of the remote player), `move` (gaps between client frames in which the remote player's position changed), `frame` (the client's own frame intervals), each with the gaps of 100 ms or more lined up with a server minute frame (within ±100 ms of it), the same against the minute frames shifted by half their spacing (`control`, about 313 ms here), and `lined_all` / `control_all` over every gap. `summaries.client_rule` applies the driver's rule to the stamp series. **The period column is the end-to-end period** (`summaries.<arm>.endPeriod`, a frame's start to the next frame's end); the artifact also carries the start-to-start `period` (`summaries.<arm>.period`), which held at 104 to 105 ms at its p99 and max in every x244c arm and 103 to 106 ms in the x244a and x244b arms; the one exception in all three sessions is a single 136 ms in x244a `burst2` (`summaries.burst2.period.max`), unexplained. The burst's busy (at most 77 ms, `summaries.burst3.busy.max`) fits inside that 100 ms cadence.

**The players were 248 tiles apart** (`phases.S0.distance`, `phases.S0.pos`: their spawn points in fixture `two`). How to read it. A ring row is sampled inside `EveryOneMinute` before the mod's queue drains that minute (the harness's `minute.ring` comment block), so a landing shows on row k and the stomach it fills on row k + 1. The hour of day is the ring row's `hour` and `min` (the age plus 7 h); chain day d runs from age 24d − 7 (00:00) to 24d + 17, so day 0 is the fixture's first day (the world opens at 10:15, age 3.25), day 1 the warm-up (maintenance) day and days 2 to 5 the request-level days; a mod day k (07:00 to 07:00, `body.eeDay`'s day) runs from age 24k to 24k + 24. `verdicts.<phase>.observed` holds each graded reading and `readings` what the driver reports beside them; `stops[*]` holds each stop (`D<day>_<hh>` a meal with its `read`, `target`, `portions`, `eaten_kcal` and `carry_out`; `<meal>_R` and `R<day>_<hhmm>` a canteen refill with its `probe`, `left_l` and `filled_l`) and `eats[*]` each portion with its `ring_s` and `ring_age`. The chain is four sessions on one world, each booting a copy of the previous session's `<run>/server` with reuse: `x282-20261011-034142` boots this run's, `x283-20261011-035042` x282's and `x284-20261011-040034` x283's; the graded rows are read from `x28-grade-20261011`.
- **The drinking (ruling T5R-1).** No water food is eaten. `autodrink.set true` runs at S, and the engine's own auto-drink (#2770) drinks from a server-side `Base.CanteenMilitaryFull` that `fluid.fill` refills to 0.9 L after every meal and at 02:00, 05:00, 10:30, 16:30 and 23:00 (`readings.refills`; a scheduled refill before the session's first stop is skipped, here R0_0200, R0_0500 and R0_1030, `verdicts.STOPS.observed.refills_skipped`). The drinks are read off the ring's `fluids.autoDrop`: a row k reading autoDrop > 0 is the sip the writer folded in drain k − 1, which drain k lands as 2 × autoDrop L of water (the lib's docstring, change 4). The replay takes each as an exogenous drink event {s: k, drink, water 2000 × autoDrop g}, the same class as the opt-in auto-drink injection. **The one-minute landing offset**: the tool lands the event before drain k's kinetics step, the server in drain k's nutrients step, so the replay's liquid lane runs one minute ahead on each drink, about 5 % of its emptying at the 13 min half-time. The auto-drink detector runs as a check only (`replay.autodrink_check`).
- **The noise sips (finding F-T5R-2).** The writer's sip fold counts any positive THIRST drop as a sip, so float noise of 3.66e-15 to 3.72e-9 in autoDrop (the four rings' range) is folded beside the real drinks: of the 840 ring rows with autoDrop > 0 here, 824 are noise and 16 are drinks of 200.03 to 201.55 g (this guide's count over the ring pages). Every count of sips, autoDrops or events is therefore a count of the noise (`readings.fluid_days.<d>.writer_sips`, `.autodrops`, `replay.autodrops.n`: do-not-cite), while the water sums are not moved (each noise event adds under 1e-5 g). The replay takes the noise events too, and it still agrees. The defect was fixed after these runs, at `5244b4a` (ruling T5R-2: `SIP_EPS` on the writer's sip fold), so these four rings carry it.
- **F-T5-2 is fixed in `x28_steady_lib.py`**: `run_phase` marks the budget and error events under `stopped_phase` and `failed_phase`, so a budget stop or a raise can no longer skip R, D and Z (`testing/tests/test_x28_steady_lib.py`); the frozen `x27_energy_lib.py` keeps the defect.
- **Maintenance** (`readings.maint_kcal`, `readings.maint_body`): the tool's maintenance 2089.32 kcal a day on fm 14.4 and lm 65.6 kg at age 6.035. Each maintenance meal targets 696.44 kcal and eats 700 (`TKX.Mixed650` and `TKX.Unit50`), the miss carried on (`readings.carry_out` −14.24); day 0's intake 1400 kcal from the two meals at 13:00 and 20:00 (`readings.live_kcal_by_day.0`).
- **The meal reads** (`readings.meal_es[i].es_read`): D0_13 1.0441, D0_20 1.0391, D1_08 1.1126 (age 25.05, after the 12 h overnight gap, awake) and D1_13 1.0485.
- **REPLAY** (`verdicts.REPLAY.observed`, `replay.diff`): from this session's start record (`start.json`, gen 1, `satiety.t` 4.168) at offset 7, ok: HUNGER max 5.77e-4, `body.energyState` 1.13e-3, `satiety.L` 0, each over n = 957 graded rows of 1771 replay rows (`replay.rows`). The ungraded rows are mostly `between` (808, a do-not-cite count): every noise autoDrop is a replay event, so the row it lands beside is classed `between` and left ungraded; the agreement rests on the 957 graded rows, not on every row. Offline 5. The replay took 807 autoDrop events, 3209.08 g of water (`replay.autodrops.water_g`). **Held in the start record** (`replay.autodrops.held_in_start`, 33 events, all noise here): every autoDrop event on a ring row up to the first row after the start record (`replay.autodrops.first_ring_s_after_start`, s 52) is held back so that none lands twice — those before it are already in the record's state, the last one pending in it. The detector alone finds 16 drinks, 3.20 L (`replay.autodrink_check.detector_alone`), and none beyond the autoDrop events.
- **STOPS** (`verdicts.STOPS.observed`): all 14 done, none missed or late, every eat landed, every refill read back. **The ring** (`verdicts.RING.observed`): 4 pages from age 3.334 to 33.684 (`readings.last_ring_age`); errors and overwritten 0.
- **SODIUM** (`verdicts.SODIUM.observed`): hyponatraemia grade 0 on chain days 0 and 1, naPlasma at least 140.07 and 140.69; the per-day sodium is read from the grade's `sodium.by_day`.

How to read it. A ring row is sampled inside `EveryOneMinute` before the mod's queue drains that minute (the harness's `minute.ring` comment block), so ring row k reads the state drain k − 1 left, and its `body.met` is what drain k − 1 billed. The hour of day is the age plus 7 h; the world opened at 10:11 (`phases.S.time.worldAge` 3.18) and the ring runs from age 3.29 to 10.27 (`readings.fluid_days.0` `first_age`, `readings.last_ring_age`). `legs[*]` holds the driver's legs in order (each with `label`, `age0`, `age1` and its `set`, `setpath` or melee record), `readings.legs[*].ring` each leg's reading off the ring (`met_max`; `met_hist`, keyed by the billed MET as a literal key, so `met_hist.1.9` is the key `1.9`; `minutes_at_or_over_6`, `S_max`, `S_rises`, `band2_rise_min`, `exKcal_rise`), and `readings.decay[0]` the decay leg against the half-life. A leg's ring reading runs from its `age0` to its `age1`, so the rest after a set is inside its leg. The graded rows are read from `x29-gate-20261011`.
- **The activity events (x29_exercise_lib change 2, a design departure).** No MET is injected live (ruling 11f-5). The replay's activity events are read off the ring: ring row k's billed `body.met` becomes an event at row k − 1 with the engine rate of the class that bills it, the class nearest the engine MET that `body.metMinDay`'s rise implies (LightWork and DefaultExercise both bill 3.0), and its exercise flag from `body.band2Day`'s rise; 14 here (`replay.activity.n`). The replay therefore reads back the mod's own billed MET: its agreement with live holds by construction for the activity term, and it tests the writer's arithmetic and integration given that billing, never whether the billing is right. The decay leg's `lua.setpath` is a replay event too (`replay.setpaths.events[0]`, s 219).
- **The gate meal** (`stops[0]`, `eats[0]`): one `TKX.Mixed650` landing at age 4.48 (ring s 73); `readings.live_kcal_by_day.0` 650. Auto-drink was set, but the gate gives no canteen and no drink landed (`replay.autodrops.n` 0).
- **IDLE** (`readings.legs[0]`, 4.53 to 4.90): 22 ring rows, all billing 1.3.
- **SQUATS** (`legs[1]`, `readings.legs[1]`): a 20-minute `exercise.do` set queued at 4.952 (`legs[1].set.age_queued`); the server showed a `FitnessExercise` at the first poll (5.019) and none at the second (5.077), so the set ended by 5.085 (`legs[1].set.age_end`), about 8 game minutes of the 20 asked (F-T6-4). Over the leg to 5.78 the ring billed at most 2.0 (`readings.legs[1].ring.met_max`; 29 rows at 1.9 and 20 at 2.0), the engine rate polled 1.88 and 2.06 (`legs[1].set.polls[0].rate`, `legs[1].set.polls[1].rate`), and S never rose (`readings.legs[1].ring.S_rises` 0). F-T6-7: 42.20.4 billed squats 3.0 to 4.0 (#2984, #3000) over a 20-minute set; this set ran 8 minutes, so no build difference is claimed.
- **BURPEES** (`legs[2]`, `readings.legs[2]`): FitnessHeavy, the heaviest exercise `exercise.do` can queue; set 5.835 to 6.085 of the 20 minutes asked; the ring billed at most 3.0 (47 rows at 2.5, 5 at 3.0), the engine rate 2.11 to 2.78 against FitnessHeavy's 9.0 target (`legs[2].set.polls[*].rate`), and S never rose. **`x29-gate-20261011/summary.json`**, **`rows.json`** and **`x291.json`** — a derived artifact: an analysis run, not a live run. Produced by `testing/experiments/x29_grade.py gate` at `fe77260` over the committed run `x291-20261011-045658` with `tools/replay_live.py` at `6575cc5` (`sleep_allowed` false, the live server's option) and `x29_exercise_lib.py` at `082fe51`; nothing is booted. **The grade's versions**: the script was committed at `082fe51` before x291's boot and amended three times, each before any grade output was committed: at `a2a4988` before x292's boot (the lag grade reads the whole day's exercise kcal; the gate output was regenerated with identical rows), at `2862968` after x292 and x293 ran and before x294's boot (F-T6-1: the stand-in starts at the activity in effect at the start record), and at `fe77260` after the chain ran (row 9 in the chain, `episodes()`); both grade folders were written at `fe77260`, and per the Task 6 report and its review the gate's rows are byte-identical across the versions, only `summary.json`'s `grade_commit` moving. Its inputs are the run's committed `gate-1.json`, `events.json`, `start.json`, `start-stats.json`, `player.json` and ring pages. `python testing/experiments/x29_grade.py gate --out <dir>` reproduces `rows.json` and `x291.json` byte for byte (re-run on 2026-10-11 into a scratch folder, `cmp` silent): `rows.json` 88469 bytes, sha256 `a6110d6e…5a8cb6ee`; `x291.json` 1667, `cf28d564…f6a4d674`. **`summary.json`** (324 bytes, `7d661933…706fd85b`) reproduces except its three short shas: it was written with 7-character abbreviations (`grade_commit` `fe77260`, `lib_commit` `082fe51`, `tool_commit` `6575cc5`), and a re-run now writes 8 (`fe772604`, `082fe51d`, `6575cc50`), git's `%h` having lengthened as the repository grew; the verdicts are identical. **Re-grading (ruling T3-1, Plan 11h)**: `x29_grade.py` stays frozen as committed, and at a HEAD after `1004bab2` (Plan 11g Task 7, which moved `K.energy.lagged` to `K.deficit.lagged`) it raises, so a re-grade runs on a `git archive` of the recorded build (the grade at `fe77260`, the mod at `5244b4a`), never on a later HEAD (Plan 11h Task 3). x29 is a pre-C-17 baseline: its mod billed a flagged minute by the engine's class, so a replay of its rings at a C-17 or later HEAD bills every flagged minute 6.0 instead (C-17's Fitness rate, and Plan 11h's fallback for a flagged minute with no recorded type), a different billing from the one x29 measured live.

How to read it. `x291.json` holds the session: `diff` (this grade's replay diff, which skips only eat, drink and setpath rows, under HUNGER 0.002, es 0.005, `satiety.L` 0.5 %, `satiety.S` 1e-6 and `body.trail.c.ex` 0.5 %) and `tool_diff` (`tools/replay_live.py`'s own, which also skips the row before every activity event), `events_by_kind`, `initial_activity` (null: nothing billed above idle at the start record) and `driver_verdicts` (copied). Inside `diff.fields` and `tool_diff.fields` the field names are literal keys with dots in them (`satiety.L`, `satiety.S`, `body.energyState`, `body.trail.c.ex`), and so are the billed MET values keying `met_hist` (`row9.legs[1].ring.met_hist.1.9` is the key `1.9`): a pointer names them as written. `rows.json` holds `row9`; `summary.json` the verdicts. As in x291's guide, the replay reads back the ring's own billed MET (x29_exercise_lib change 2), so the replay's S and HUNGER agreement holds by construction for the activity term and tests the writer's arithmetic, never the billing.
- **The gate legs** (`row9.legs[i]`; `summary.json` `verdicts.VIGOUR`): IDLE 22 rows at 1.3; SQUATS queued 4.952, ended 5.085 (`row9.legs[1].set.age_queued`, `.age_end`), the ring billing at most 2.0 (`row9.legs[1].ring.met_max`), the engine rate at most 2.059 (`row9.legs[1].set.rate_max`), S rises 0 (`row9.legs[1].ring.S_rises`); BURPEES 5.835 to 6.085, at most 3.0, the rate at most 2.776, S rises 0; MELEE 0 windows, 25 misses, 2 hordes (`row9.legs[4].melee.windows`, `.misses`, `.hordes`): **unmeasured**. No candidate was vigorous (`verdicts.VIGOUR` false for all three): the rise leg is unmeasured in the gate (ruling 11f-5; ruling T6-1), and measured once in the chain (`x29-lag-20261011` `row9_chain`). The HeavyWork actions were not run (no harness command). `row9.legs[3]` and `[4]` at rest carry the burpees' billing tail (1.9 to 2.0, then 1.6; `exKcal_rise` 54.06 and 57.56; F-T6-2).
- **The decay leg** (`row9.decay[0]`; `summary.json` `verdicts.DECAY_HALF_LIFE`, `.DECAY_FACTOR`): after `satiety.S` was set to 1 at rest (`row9.decay[0].event`, s 219; `age_set` 6.935), S followed 0.5^((t − t_e)/0.15) within 8.88e-16 relative over 119 graded rows (`row9.decay[0].max_rel`, `.graded`; `row9.half_life_h` 0.15) and the replay of live within 1.11e-16 (`.replay_S_max_diff`); the written HUNGER over the no-acute replay's (the same replay with `K.satiety.ACUTE_MAX` 0) matched 1 − 0.7·S within 5.86e-5 relative over 61 uncapped rows (`row9.decay[0].factor.max_rel`, `.factor.graded`), and within 6.08e-5 over the 89 rows of the session with S > 1e-3 (`row9.factor_all_S_over_1e-3`). 30 game minutes after the set S read 0.09920 (`S_30min_after_set`; predicted 0.099) and live HUNGER sat 3.45 mm under the no-acute replay (`mm_30min_after_set`, −3.4476, at 260 mm a unit, ruling 11c-31's assumed mapping).

**`x29-lag-20261011/summary.json`**, **`rows.json`**, **`x292.json`**, **`x293.json`**, **`x294.json`**, **`x295.json`** and **`x296.json`** — a derived artifact: an analysis run, not a live run. How to read it. Chain day d runs from age 24d − 7 (00:00) to 24d + 17; bout B<d> starts at 15:00 on day d (age 24d + 8). Each `x29N.json` holds one session as `x29-gate`'s `x291.json` does, plus `lag_agreement` and `initial_activity`: for x293 and x295 the activity in effect at the start record (UsingTools, rate 2.5), with which the grade's stand-in starts (F-T6-1); null where the session attached at idle. The dotted field names are literal keys (`lag_agreement.satiety.L.max_rel`, `diff.fields.body.trail.c.ex.max`, `row10.bouts[0].met_hist.2.5`, `drinking_sodium.by_day.7.fluids.na_end`): a pointer names them as written. `rows.json` holds `row10`, `row9_chain` and `drinking_sodium`; `summary.json` the verdicts.
- **What row 10's agreement tests.** The replay's activity events are the mod's own billed MET read back off the ring (x29_exercise_lib change 2), so the agreement of `satiety.L`, es and `body.trail.c.ex` with the replay holds by construction for the activity term. What it does test is the time integration of the lag and of the energy state, the eat and drink inputs, the record carried across each restart (each session's replay starts from its own start record) and the writer's arithmetic. It never tests whether the billing is right: F-T6-2 (the tail, below), F-T6-3 (no normal set reaches vigour) and mechanism candidate C-2 are the readings of that.
- **Row 10, the agreement** (`row10.agreement.<s>.<field>.max_rel`, `.n`, `.ok`; `summary.json` `verdicts.LAG_AGREEMENT`): rel with a floor of 1, every row graded but the eat, drink and setpath rows and the offline rows. `satiety.L` 9.75e-5, 8.8e-7, 7.0e-7, 5.1e-7 and 1.9e-8; es 1.62e-3, 1.21e-3, 8.0e-4, 7.9e-4 and 8.2e-4; `body.trail.c.ex` 6.53e-5, 3.2e-6, 1.5e-6, 3.3e-6 and 1.4e-7 (x292 to x296), over 1739, 2010, 1996, 2004 and 1940 rows; all inside 0.5 %. x293's and x295's pass only with F-T6-1's start rate; their in-driver REPLAY verdicts read falsified (`driver_verdicts`, do-not-cite; the runs' guides). The session diffs (`x29N.json` `diff`, `tool_diff`; `summary.json` `verdicts.REPLAY_OK`) are ok in both forms, HUNGER at most 6.99e-4.
- **The bouts** (`row10.bouts[i]`): `kcal_ring` is `body.exKcalDay`'s rise from the bout's start to 15 game minutes past its stop: 300.04, 250.41, 252.19, 298.15, 261.58, 257.22 and 262.63 kcal (B0 to B6; `row10.series.mean_bout_kcal` 268.89). Every window billed at most 5.0 with no minute at 6.0 (`met_max`, `minutes_at_or_over_6`) **except that B0's numbers are its window only**: its set never ended at the stop and ran on to 9.83, billing 6.0 on 10 rows from 9.668 (F-T6-4, the episode below), outside the window to 9.42; B0's `met_max`, `minutes_at_or_over_6`, `S_max` and `met_hist` are do-not-cite as the bout's, and its `kcal_ring` is the window's billing, not the bout's. B3's set also ran past its stop, to 81.31, inside its window. `sets_started` 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2.
- **The post-exercise billing tail (F-T6-2): a probable billing-accuracy defect, pending a fix** (ruling T6-2; mechanism candidate C-17). `row10.series.ex_kcal_by_day.<d>.kcal` sums every rise of `body.exKcalDay` over the chain day (all billing above the idle 1.3; the 07:00 reset row's rise is lost, `resets`): 856.83, 644.71, 774.59, 865.92, 634.83 and 641.46 kcal on the complete days 1 to 6, 3.42, 2.56, 2.60, 3.31, 2.47 and 2.44 times the day's bout window (`row10.bouts[d].kcal_ring`; this guide's arithmetic): the bout's window is a third or less of the day's billed exercise. After every bout the ring billed 1.9 to 2.0 for about an hour, then 1.6, and returned to the idle 1.3 at `ex_kcal_by_day.<d>.tail_back_to_idle_age` 39.95, 62.84, 87.20, 111.99, 134.83 and 158.79 on days 1 to 6, 6.83, 5.71, 6.03, 6.83, 5.66 and 5.62 h after the bout's stop (`row10.bouts[d].age1`; this guide's arithmetic). **Days 1 and 4 straddle a session-attach gap that fell inside the tail** (ring empty from 33.684 to 34.769 and from 105.735 to 106.850, both sides billing 4.0): `body.exKcalDay` rose 246.82 and 253.69 kcal across the empty ring, 29 % of each day's sum, and their 6.83 h includes the 1.1 h gap (this guide's reading of the rings); the grade's `hours` counts the step across the gap, so those days read `complete` true. Without the gap rise days 1 and 4 read 2.44 and 2.34 times their bout; the four gap-free days 5.62 to 6.03 h. Real excess post-exercise oxygen consumption is far smaller than 2.4 to 3.4 times a bout; the mod change waits for the sedentary live tasks, an EPOC science harvest and a read-only investigation of the billing tail run first, and row 10 re-runs after the fix (ruling T6-2). Whether the engine rate itself stays raised is inferred from the billing class (the polls read the rate only during sets).
- **L and the share** (`row10.series.by_day[d]`, `row10.series.reading_7_days_after_first_bout`): at each day's end (age 24d + 17) L reads 60.62, 109.61, 142.55, 181.49, 223.71, 249.13 and 273.44 and es 1.1229, 1.0147, 1.0227, 1.0305, 1.0287, 1.0389 and 1.0474 (days 0 to 6). lagged(L) is `K.energy.lagged`, 0.7 × L. - **The share is a reading, and its distances are named, not graded.** (1) **The denominator**: the grade's mean is over the complete days 1 to 6. Day 0 is partial only in the idle morning before the world opened (the ring starts at 10:14, before B0) and holds B0 and its overrun whole, 986.68 kcal (`ex_kcal_by_day.0`, do-not-cite); with it the mean over days 0 to 6 is 772.15 and the share about 0.238, 0.99 times the arm (this guide's arithmetic), against 0.2500, 1.039 times, over days 1 to 6. The whole-day denominator is the like-for-like one with the arm, whose exercise kcal is its whole bout, while live's includes the tail. (2) **Feeding**: the arm eats the idle day plus its whole bout; live eats a third of the tool's maintenance 2089.32 plus a third of the bout's window read at the stop (191 to 224 kcal) per meal, below an awake idle day's billing (about 2280, x28-grade) and without the tail, so the live body ran a deficit (es 1.015 to 1.047 at the ends of days 1 to 6). (3) **The bout's shape**: the arm's 53 minutes at 9.5 at 02:00, 834 kcal; live's 60-minute burpee window at 15:00, billed at most 5.0 (B0's overrun aside), 250 to 300 kcal in the window and the tail after it, and on days 1 and 4 the attach-gap billing. As in row 10, the replay reads back the billed MET and band2Day, so the step's match tests the writer's arithmetic given that billing. The episode came 1.58 h after the set was queued (`first_age` less x292's `readings.bouts[0].sets[0].age_queued`); its shape (10 resistance rows from S 0) is not the oracle's 60-minute aerobic bout (0.674, −3.7 mm), so the distance is named, not graded. No other session had an episode (`row9_chain.episodes.x293` to `.x296` empty).

How to read it. A ring row is sampled inside `EveryOneMinute` before the mod's queue drains that minute (the harness's `minute.ring` comment block), so ring row k reads the state drain k − 1 left. The hour of day is the age plus 7 h, and every ring row carries its own `hour` and `min`; the world opened at 10:11 (`phases.S.time.worldAge` 3.18), the record was created at its first sight at age 3.10 (`start.json` `rec.firstSeen` 3.1017513275146484, 10:06), and the ring runs from age 3.319 to 55.718 (`readings.fluid_days.0.first_age`, `readings.last_ring_age`) over 31 paths (`phases.H.ring_paths`), among them the record's sleep state `acute.debtH`, `acute.sleptH`, `acute.winSleptH`, `acute.winStartH`, `acute.awakeH`, `acute.boutH` and `acute.S`. The calendar (x30_sleep_lib): day 0's maintenance meals at 13:00 and 20:00, each a third of the tool's maintenance 2089.32 kcal (`readings.maint_kcal`, on fm 14.4 and lm 65.6 kg at age 6.03, `readings.maint_body`, read once here and carried by the chain); request meals at 08:00, 13:00 and 20:00 on days 1 to 4, each sized by the es read and the hour (§ 3.7 form 1), never by the sleep factor, whole portions with the miss carried on; the nights N0 (rested, 7.5 h, from 21:45 on day 0) and N1 (short, 5.5 h, from 00:15 on day 2) in this session, N2 (recovery, 9.5 h, from 20:30 on day 2) and N3 (rested, 7.5 h, from 21:45 on day 3) in x302; canteen refills at 10:30, at 16:30 and after every meal and night. Chain day d runs from age 24d − 7 (00:00) to 24d + 17. `stops[*]` holds each stop: `D<day>_<hh>` a meal (`read`, `target`, `portions`, `eaten_kcal`, `carry_out`), `N<k>` a night (`before`, `hold`, `polls`, `cancel`, `settle`, `after`, `age0`, `age1`, `booked_h`, `held_h`), `<stop>_R` and `R<day>_<hhmm>` a refill. The chain is two sessions on one world: `x302-20261011-091000` boots a copy of this run's `<run>/server` with reuse; the graded rows are read from `x30-grade-20261011` and the tool's fixed diff from `x30-regrade-20261011`.
- **The nights: held sleep stopped on the booked sleep (x30_sleep_lib change 3, a design departure named before the run)** (`stops[6]`, `stops[16]`, `readings.nights[0]`, `[1]`; `verdicts.NIGHTS`): at speed 1, `player.sleep.hold admin 600` holds the player asleep; the driver polls the record's `acute.winSleptH` and, once the sleep booked since the night's start plus the booking rate times one round trip reaches the target, sends `player.sleep.hold admin 0` and then `player.sleep admin false` (`cancel.reason` `target`). A night's length is therefore its booked sleep, not its held span: about 15 % of held minutes run awake (#2840), so a held 7.5 h would leave a rested night short. N0 booked 7.6950 h over a held span of 9.1655 h (`booked_over_held` 0.8396); N1 booked 5.6456 h over 6.7678 h (0.8342). The held span (`age0` to `age1`) runs from the first poll's drain to the read after the cancel's and the wake's round trips and the settle reads; `game_h_per_wall_s` (0.516 and 0.534) is that span over the wall seconds from the hold to the wake's reply (`cancel.wall_since_hold`): about 20 times the speed-1 clock of 1.6 game minutes a wall second, the cancel's round trips counted in it. The unbroken asleep run `acute.sleptH` reached at most 0.373 h in a night (the hold's flag flickers; this guide's reading of the ring) while `acute.boutH` reached the booked sleep (`stops[6].after.boutH` 7.6950, `stops[16].after.boutH` 5.6456).
- **The overshoot (F-T7-2)** (`readings.nights[i].miss_h`): N0 +0.195 h, N1 +0.146 h. The one-round-trip lead was too short: the night ends only after the cancel and the wake land, two more round trips. C1's debt is therefore 1.8544 h, not the oracle's 2.0. `verdicts.NIGHTS` reads as_predicted on its own rule: each night stopped by the target rule, inside one window, booked within 0.25 h of its target.
- **The closes and the debt (F-T7-3; mechanism candidate C-18)** (`readings.closes[0]`, `[1]`; `verdicts.CLOSES`): the record's 24 h windows run from its creation (`readings.closes[0].win_start_before` 3.1018), so each closes at 10:06 to 10:07 (the ring rows' own `hour` and `min` at `s_before` 1054 and 2219, `s_after` 1055 and 2220). C0 at age 27.118 booked N0's 7.6950 h and left a debt of 0; C1 at 51.118 booked N1's 5.6456 h and left 1.8544 h (`booked_h`, `debt_after`). Each equals the kernel's booking, clamp(debt + max(0, 7.5 − booked) − 0.5 × max(0, booked − 7.5), 0, 40) (`debt_kernel`, `kernel_diff` 0.0), and the replay's debt (`debt_replay`, `replay_diff` 0). The debt reaches hunger at the close, not at waking: N1 woke at 48.08 (`marks[1].age`), D2_08's read at 49.04 saw a debt of 0, and the debt arrived at C1, about 3 h after waking (the grade's `row11.meals[5]`). `verdicts.CLOSES` grades only that each close equals the kernel's booking and the replay's within 1e-6; its predicted bands are driver text.
- **The sleep events, and what the replay's sleep agreement tests.** The replay's sleep events are read off the ring (x30_sleep_lib change 4): drain k ran asleep when ring row k + 1 reads `acute.sleptH` > 0, and the event {s: k, sleep} is due before drain k (90 here, 45 of them asleep; `replay.sleep_events`). The replay therefore takes its asleep minutes from live: its `acute.winSleptH` and `acute.debtH` agreeing with live checks the booking arithmetic (the window's sum and the close's formula) **by construction**, never whether the mod detects sleep. HUNGER, es, L and the sleep factor stay independent readings (the grade).
- **The drinking (ruling T5R-1)**, as x28's and x29's chains: `autodrink.set true` at S; the engine's own auto-drink drinks from a server-side `Base.CanteenMilitaryFull` that `fluid.fill` refills to 0.9 L (`readings.refills`); a ring row reading `fluids.autoDrop` > 0 is a drink given to the replay as an exogenous drink event with the one-minute landing offset. The replay took 28 autoDrop events, 5830.75 g (`replay.autodrops.n`, `.water_g`); the detector alone finds 28 drinks, 5.80 L, none beyond them (`replay.autodrink_check`). The engine drank inside the held nights too: 5 autoDrop events inside N0's held span and 3 inside N1's (this guide's reading of `events.json` against `age0` and `age1`). Day 1 is the session's one whole day: 2662.1 g on the mod side (`readings.fluid_days.1.drunk_g_mod`; the grade's `drinking_sodium.by_day.1.mod_l`).
- **The meals** (`readings.meal_es`, `stops`): D0_13 reads es 1.0445 at age 6.03, targets 696.44 and eats 700; D0_20 1.0397, eats 700; D1_08 1.0835 (after the first night), targets 648.48, eats 650; D1_13 1.0224, eats 650; D1_20 1.0191, targets 719.74, eats 700; D2_08 1.0279, targets 612.72, eats 650; D2_13 1.0297, targets 659.50, eats 650; day 1's intake 2000 kcal (`readings.live_kcal_by_day.1`).

**`x30-grade-20261011/summary.json`**, **`rows.json`**, **`x301.json`** and **`x302.json`** — a derived artifact: an analysis run, not a live run. Produced by `testing/experiments/x30_grade.py`, committed at `457df8c0` before x301's boot and not amended, over the two committed runs `x301-20261011-085950` and `x302-20261011-091000` with `tools/replay_live.py` at `b4b9a298` (`sleep_allowed` true, the live server's option; the activity from the ring's rate and exe, the tool's default) and `x30_sleep_lib.py` at `457df8c0`; nothing is booted. Its inputs are each run's committed `sleep-N.json`, `events.json`, `start.json`, `start-stats.json`, `player.json` and ring pages. Run on a `git archive` of `457df8c0` with the two run folders copied in (on 2026-10-11 into a scratch folder), it reproduces `rows.json` (26108 bytes, sha256 `17c93d8b…9a1b9c8f`), `x301.json` (2341, `664ee1d6…177d773f`) and `x302.json` (2339, `51fda239…dcdd09d0`) byte for byte (`cmp` silent); **`summary.json`** (656 bytes, `678da9d1…ae8cddea`) reproduces except its three commit fields, which the archive, holding no git history, writes empty (`grade_commit` and `lib_commit` `457df8c0`, `tool_commit` `b4b9a298`); the verdicts are identical. Run at a later HEAD the script takes the fixed tool, so its `tool_diff` would differ: this folder is the `b4b9a298` tool's output.

How to read it. Each `x30N.json` holds one session: `diff` (this grade's replay diff, which skips only the eat and drink rows, `between` 38 and 43, under HUNGER 0.002, es 0.005, `satiety.L` 0.5 %, `acute.debtH` 1e-6 and `acute.winSleptH` 1e-6; a sleep event changes what the next drain books, so no ring row sits between it and its effect), `tool_diff` (the tool's own, on 0 rows by F-T7-1), `events_by_kind` (drink 28 and 25, eat 10 and 18, sleep 90 and 118), `ring_activity_events`, `sleep_events`, `asleep_agreement`, `guard` and `driver_verdicts` (copied). A `gap` row in a diff is a long minute: the next ring row's `dtM` exceeds 2.05 game minutes (`replay_live.link_marks`), here the fast-forwarded rows of the held nights (`dtM` 3.16 to 3.67, this guide's reading of the rings); a gap row is graded and its findings marked. Inside `diff.fields` the field names are literal keys with dots in them (`acute.debtH`, `satiety.L`), and so are `drinking_sodium.by_day.<d>.fluids.na_end` and the like: a pointer names them as written. `rows.json` holds `row11` and `drinking_sodium`; `summary.json` the verdicts. Chain day d runs from age 24d − 7 to 24d + 17.
- **What the agreement tests.** The replay's sleep events are live's own asleep minutes read off `acute.sleptH` (x301's guide), so the agreement of `acute.winSleptH` and `acute.debtH` with live (`diff.fields.acute.winSleptH.max`, `diff.fields.acute.debtH.max`, 0.0 in both sessions) and the closes' `replay_diff` check the booking arithmetic by construction, not sleep detection. HUNGER, es, L and the sleep factor are independent: `diff.fields.HUNGER.max` 0.00115 and 0.00172, `diff.fields.body.energyState.max` 0.00184 and 0.00161, `satiety.L` 0.0, over n = 2403 and 1816 graded rows (`diff.fields.<f>.n`), of which 289 and 377 are gap rows (`diff.classes.gap`). On the rows after an asleep drain (`asleep_agreement.rows` 252 and 330) HUNGER agrees within 0.00115 and 0.00129 and es within 0.00176 and 0.00155.
- **The nights** (`row11.nights[i]`; `summary.json` `verdicts.NIGHTS_AT_TARGET`): N0 to N3 targets 7.5, 5.5, 9.5 and 7.5 h booked 7.6950, 5.6456, 9.7270 and 7.7136 h (`booked_h`) over held spans of 9.1655, 6.7678, 11.4915 and 9.2338 h (`held_h`), shares 0.8396, 0.8342, 0.8465 and 0.8354 (`booked_over_held`), overshoots +0.195, +0.146, +0.227 and +0.214 h (`miss_h`, F-T7-2), fast-forward 0.516 to 0.535 game h per wall second (`game_h_per_wall_s`, x301's guide's definition). **`NIGHTS_AT_TARGET` true means "stopped by the target rule"** (`reason` `target`: the booked sleep plus one round trip's lead reached the target), not that the booked sleep equals the target: every night overshot.

**`x32-grade-20261011/summary.json`**, **`rows.json`**, **`x321.json`**, **`x322.json`** and **`x323.json`** — a derived artifact: an analysis run, not a live run. Produced by `testing/experiments/x32_grade.py`, committed at `2fe18691` before x321's boot and not amended, over the three committed runs `x321-20261011-102913`, `x322-20261011-103758` and `x323-20261011-104618` with `tools/replay_live.py` as at `2fe18691` (its last change `51e6b2e9`; `sleep_allowed` false, the live server's option; the activity from the ring's rate and exe, the stat NICOTINE_WITHDRAWAL fed from each ring row) and `x32_nicotine_lib.py` at `2fe18691`; nothing is booted. Its inputs are each run's committed `nicotine-N.json`, `events.json`, `start.json`, `start-stats.json`, `player.json` and ring pages. Run on a `git archive` of `2fe18691` with the three run folders copied in (on 2026-10-11 into a scratch folder), it reproduces `rows.json` (28711 bytes, sha256 `94f243fe…bfd8a277`), `x321.json` (2140, `662b2262…5860609f`), `x322.json` (2034, `d299cd57…ac76d5bf`) and `x323.json` (2328, `d0a23dab…fe67ac3e`) byte for byte (`cmp` silent); **`summary.json`** (904 bytes, `e31571c2…eba7bd8c`) reproduces except its three commit fields, which the archive, holding no git history, writes empty (`grade_commit` and `lib_commit` `2fe18691`, `tool_commit` `51e6b2e9`); the verdicts are identical.

How to read it. Each `x32N.json` holds one session: `diff` (this grade's replay diff, which skips a row only for an eat, a drink, a smoke or seed marker, or a row an anchor edit's timing holds, `held_rows` 29, 26 and 33, under HUNGER 0.002, es 0.005, `satiety.L` 0.5 % and `satiety.nicH` one game minute), `tool_diff` (the tool's own), `events_by_kind`, `regimes` (the ring rows of the seed, the smokes and the edits), `drain_skew`, `guard`, `ring_activity_events` and `driver_verdicts` (copied). Inside `diff.fields` the field names are literal keys with dots in them (`satiety.nicH`, `body.energyState`), and so are `drinking_sodium.by_day.<d>.fluids.na_end` and the like: a pointer names them as written. `rows.json` holds `row12` and `drinking_sodium`; `summary.json` the verdicts. Chain day d runs from age 24d − 7 to 24d + 17. The design departures are x321's guide's; the oracle's study agreement is not re-tested live (ruling 8-R: live against the replay shows the mechanics hold in the live game, and a live match to a study is by construction wherever the constant was fitted to that study).
- **What the agreement tests.** The replay is fed the live stat w from each ring row, so the withdrawal itself (its threshold, rate and cap) is the engine's and is never tested against the replay; it is read off the ring (below). The anchor agrees exactly (`diff.fields.satiety.nicH.max` 0.0 in all three sessions) **by construction**: the replay runs the same writer on the same fed w at the same drain ages, the live drain's own age equal to the ring row before it on every online row (`drain_skew.max_m` 0.0 in all three; `min_m` and `mean_m`, do-not-cite, take in the 3 or 4 offline rows after each quit, where the drain does not run, −1.0 to −4.08 game min, this guide's reading of the rings' `on` flag). HUNGER, es and L are independent: `diff.fields.HUNGER.max` 0.00049, 0.00068 and 0.00032, `diff.fields.body.energyState.max` 0.00115, 0.00119 and 0.00113, `satiety.L` 0.0, over n = 2042, 2012 and 1582 graded rows (`diff.fields.<f>.n`), `diff.ok` true in all three.

**`x33-grade-20261011/summary.json`**, **`rows.json`**, **`x331.json`**, **`x332.json`** and **`x333.json`** — a derived artifact: an analysis run, not a live run. Produced by `testing/experiments/x33_grade.py`, committed at `6a6cdb61` before x331's boot and not amended, over the three committed runs `x331-20261011-140738`, `x332-20261011-141601` and `x333-20261011-142329` with `tools/replay_live.py` as at `6a6cdb61` (its last change `51e6b2e9`; `sleep_allowed` false, the live server's option; the activity from the ring's rate and exe; the autoDrop drink events and the setany values as stat events) and `x33_monotony_lib.py` at `6a6cdb61`; nothing is booted. Its inputs are each run's committed `monotony-N.json`, `events.json`, `start.json`, `start-stats.json`, `player.json` and ring pages. Run on a `git archive` of `6a6cdb61` with the three run folders copied in (on 2026-10-11 into a scratch folder), it reproduces `rows.json` (37055 bytes, sha256 `a64f7558…23258390`), `x331.json` (1772, `fa57a27e…0676fc5f`), `x332.json` (4265, `6ca59e8e…c07741de`) and `x333.json` (4627, `c17efeaf…21ad6a3f`) byte for byte (`cmp` silent); **`summary.json`** (1130 bytes, `d87c80a8…f05ad6a0`) reproduces except its three commit fields, which the archive, holding no git history, writes empty (`grade_commit` and `lib_commit` `6a6cdb61`, `tool_commit` `51e6b2e9`); the verdicts are identical.

How to read it. Each `x33N.json` holds one session: `tool_diff` (the tool's own replay diff, HUNGER 0.002, es 0.005, `satiety.L` 0.5 %; this grade has no diff of its own), `unhappy_vs_replay` (auxiliary, do-not-cite), `events_by_kind`, `ring_activity_events`, `rows`, `ring_first_age`, `ring_last_age` and `driver_verdicts` (copied). Inside `tool_diff.fields` the field names are literal keys with dots in them (`body.energyState`, `satiety.L`), and so are `drinking_sodium.by_day.<d>.fluids.na_end` and the like: a pointer names them as written. `rows.json` holds `row13` and `drinking_sodium`; `summary.json` the verdicts. Chain day d runs from age 24d − 7 to 24d + 17. The design departures are x331's guide's, and **these runs describe the add design at `35c3049e`, which ruling T9-1 replaced after them with the self-limiting mood floor (Task 9b)**. The oracle's agreement with its study is not re-tested live (ruling 8-R: live against the kernel and the replay shows the mechanics hold in the live game, and a live match to a pin is by construction wherever the constant was fitted to it).
- **The eats** (`row13.eats[i]`, i from 0 to 9 in the order M0, S0, M1, S1, M2, S2, M3, S3, M4, S4: `label`, `session`, `day`, `food`, `staple`, `n_before`, `n_after`, `last_before`, `last_after`, `pre`, `post`, `pre_age`, `post_age`, `add`, `add_minus_kernel`, `n_after_minus_kernel`, `replay`, `replay_minus_add`, `client_before`, `client_first_add`, `client_reads`, `monotony_counter_rose`, `set`, `window`). The UNHAPPINESS adds read 0, 0, 3.4121532440185547, 0.8530616760253906, 6.121330261230469, 1.5311717987060547, 8.270425796508789, 2.067424774169922, 9.975353240966797 and 2.4946537017822266 (`row13.eats[i].add.UNHAPPINESS`); `add_minus_kernel.UNHAPPINESS` at most 1.07e-6 in size and `n_after_minus_kernel` 0.0 at every eat. **What that agreement is**: the kernel's delta (`kernel_delta`, do-not-cite) is the grade's arithmetic on the live record's entry, so the agreement is by construction on the formula; it tests the add's `Stats.add` landing on the server with nothing taking it back before the post read, w = 1, `isStaple` (the staple's quarter slope), the entry's persistence across the two restarts (`n_before` at M2, S2, M3 and S3 equal to the previous session's `n_after`), and the booked age inside the read pair (`last_after` between `pre_age` and `post_age` at all ten eats).

Idle BOREDOM in those holds peaked at 27.27 and 29.16 (`bored_max`), BORED level 1, so **vanilla's unhappiness term while the BORED level is above 1 (`BodyDamage.UpdateBoredom @510–@575`, the levels of #2369) was not exercised**; real play with BOREDOM above 50 would climb faster than this sum. The projections (`projection_one_a_day`, `projection_three_a_day`, `steady_daily_add`, the days to 100) are offline kernel arithmetic, never a measurement, and are do-not-cite.
